issues.claim: PlayOn violated the CCPA's prohibition on selling or sharing personal information of consumers aged 13-16 without affirmative opt-in consent
issues.issue: Multiple authoritative law firm analyses (Loeb & Loeb, Richt Law Firm) state that 'the decision did not find that PlayOn Sports violated any of the special protections provided to teens or children under California law.' The settlement requires future compliance with minor-specific provisions, but the CPPA did not make a finding that PlayOn violated Section 1798.120(c)'s prohibition on selling/sharing minors' data without opt-in consent. The report presents a forward-looking compliance requirement as a found violation, which materially mischaracterizes the enforcement decision.
issues.suggested_fix: Revise to: 'The settlement requires PlayOn to comply with the CCPA's prohibition on selling or sharing personal information of consumers aged 13-16 without affirmative opt-in consent, though the decision did not make a specific finding that PlayOn violated these minor-specific protections.'

issues.claim: PlayOn's privacy notice had not been updated for over a year
issues.issue: Multiple sources (WilmerHale, Holland & Knight, Inside Privacy) report that PlayOn's privacy policy had not been updated since July 2022, meaning it was outdated for approximately 2.5 years by the end of the violation period (December 2024). Stating 'over a year' is technically true but significantly understates the duration and diminishes the severity of the notice deficiency.
issues.suggested_fix: Revise to: 'PlayOn's privacy notice had not been updated since July 2022 — over two and a half years — failing to meet the CCPA requirement to update privacy policies at least annually.'

issues.claim: the CPPA ruled this does not satisfy CCPA requirements under Cal. Civ. Code Section 1798.120
issues.issue: The inline text references 'Cal. Civ. Code Section 1798.120' (the consumer's right to opt out of sale) but the hyperlink URL points to FindLaw's page for Section 1798.135 (business obligations for providing opt-out mechanisms). While both sections are relevant, the mismatch between text and URL is confusing. Section 1798.135 (the linked page) is arguably more directly relevant to the business obligation to provide opt-out mechanisms.
issues.suggested_fix: Either update the link text to reference Section 1798.135 (which matches the URL), or update the URL to point to the Section 1798.120 page (https://codes.findlaw.com/ca/civil-code/civ-sect-1798-120/) to match the text. Consider referencing both sections for completeness.
